title: Glycogen Storage Disorders: Differentiating Classic Types
subject: Biochemistry
preview: Type I glycogen storage disease (von Gierke) involves glucose-6-phosphatase system dysfunction and fasting hypoglycemia.
quickRevision: Type I glycogen storage disease (von Gierke) involves glucose-6-phosphatase system dysfunction and fasting hypoglycemia.
Type V (McArdle) is muscle glycogen phosphorylase deficiency associated with exercise intolerance.
Differentiate by tissue affected, fasting response, muscle symptoms and enzyme defect rather than the shared word glycogen.

sections.title: Core biomedical mechanism
points: Type I glycogen storage disease (von Gierke) involves glucose-6-phosphatase system dysfunction and fasting hypoglycemia.
Type II (Pompe) is lysosomal acid alpha-glucosidase deficiency associated with cardiomyopathy or myopathy.

sections.title: Clinical application
points: Type V (McArdle) is muscle glycogen phosphorylase deficiency associated with exercise intolerance.
Differentiate by tissue affected, fasting response, muscle symptoms and enzyme defect rather than the shared word glycogen.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Pompe disease is a lysosomal disorder rather than simply a hepatic glycogen mobilization defect.
